case-1.objects: A probability measure μ on E, a real constant C, real-valued smooth compactly supported test functions v, and a real-valued smooth compactly supported function f. For a real-valued g let m_g = ∫ g dμ. The conclusion uses variance ∫ (f − m_f)^2 dμ and Dirichlet energy ∫ ‖∇f‖² dμ, with the genuine inner-product gradient ∇.
case-1.domains: E is an implicitly quantified type carrying a normed additive commutative group structure, a real inner product space structure, completeness, finite dimension over ℝ, a measurable space structure, and the BorelSpace compatibility instance. μ is a measure on this Borel space with an IsProbabilityMeasure instance. Both f and the tests v map E to ℝ. All displayed integrals are against μ over E.
case-1.quantifiers: For every E with the listed typeclass instances, every μ with the probability instance, and every C : ℝ, if the displayed log-Sobolev bound holds for every v : E → ℝ that is C∞ and has compact support, then for every f : E → ℝ that is C∞ and has compact support the stated conjunction holds. The same C and μ are used throughout.
case-1.assumptions: The log-Sobolev hypothesis is ∫ v(x)^2 log(v(x)^2) dμ(x) − (∫ v(x)^2 dμ(x)) log(∫ v(x)^2 dμ(x)) ≤ 2 C ∫ ‖∇v(x)‖² dμ(x) for every C∞ compactly supported v. Independently, f is C∞ and has compact support. There is no separate admissibility assumption on f, no assumption of a density for μ, and no explicit sign assumption on C.
case-1.conclusion: Both Poincare.Admissible μ f and Poincare.variance μ f ≤ C · Poincare.dirichletEnergy μ f hold. Admissibility says that f, x ↦ (f(x) − ∫ f dμ)^2, and x ↦ ‖∇f(x)‖² are each μ-integrable. In particular the inequality is ∫ (f − ∫ f dμ)^2 dμ ≤ C ∫ ‖∇f‖² dμ with the stated integrability, not merely an inequality between totalized integral expressions.
case-1.senses: C∞ means real Fréchet smoothness at every finite order, not analyticity. Compact support is compactness of the closure of the nonzero set. The log is the real natural logarithm, with the entropy terms using the zero convention (including the zero test). The centered variance is taken under μ, and the gradient is the genuine gradient defined by the inner product, not a weak or metric slope. The conclusion concerns smooth compactly supported f only; it does not extend the inequality to every admissible f or assert a converse.
case-1.constants: The real parameter C appears as 2 C in the entropy inequality and exactly C in the Poincaré inequality. No separate positivity, optimality, or sharpness of C is asserted.

case-2.objects: A probability measure μ on X; a real-valued function f on X; a real bound M; a real perturbation parameter e; and ν(e) = μ.withDensity(x ↦ ENNReal.ofReal(1 + e f(x))). The divergence is InformationTheory.klDiv(ν(e), μ) in that order, with extended nonnegative real values; the expansion uses its toReal value.
case-2.domains: X is an implicitly quantified type with a MeasurableSpace instance, with no required topology, vector space, or Borel structure. μ is a measure on X with an IsProbabilityMeasure instance. f : X → ℝ and M, e : ℝ. The density takes values in the extended nonnegative reals and the asymptotic uses the real neighborhood filter 𝓝 (0 : ℝ).
case-2.quantifiers: For every X with the listed measurable structure, every probability μ on X, every f : X → ℝ satisfying the hypotheses, and every implicit M : ℝ witnessing the bound, define ν for all real e. There is a neighborhood of zero on which each e simultaneously gives a probability ν(e) and finite divergence. Separately, the little-o claim quantifies over every tolerance η > 0 with a possibly η-dependent neighborhood of zero.
case-2.assumptions: f is μ-almost-everywhere strongly measurable, |f(x)| ≤ M for μ-almost every x, and its integral ∫ f dμ equals zero. Neither everywhere measurability nor a pointwise bound is assumed. Boundedness together with the probability and measurability assumptions makes f and f² integrable; no separate integrability, positivity of M, or nonzero second moment is assumed.
case-2.conclusion: Both claims hold: (1) eventually for e in 𝓝 0, ν(e) is a probability measure and klDiv(ν(e), μ) < ⊤; (2) the real residual r(e) = klDiv(ν(e), μ).toReal − e²[(∫ f(x)² dμ(x))/2] satisfies r = o[𝓝 0](e ↦ e²). Equivalently in the eventual probability and finite-divergence regime, the ordinary KL divergence has the expansion e²(∫ f² dμ)/2 + o(e²).
case-2.senses: withDensity is relative to μ and ENNReal.ofReal clips negative real values to zero, so the definition does not assume an everywhere nonnegative untruncated affine density. Near zero, essential boundedness does make 1 + e f positive μ-almost everywhere, and centering yields unit mass. The neighborhood is two-sided and includes zero. The little-o statement means that for each η > 0, |r(e)| ≤ η |e|² eventually in that full neighborhood, hence r(e)/e² tends to zero on the punctured neighborhood as well. Only eventual finiteness makes toReal an ordinary finite KL value there; the proposition gives no all-e probability or finiteness claim, exact quadratic identity, uniform asymptotic over f, or higher-order bound.
case-2.constants: M is a real essential absolute bound, not the expansion coefficient. The quadratic coefficient is exactly (∫ f² dμ)/2, half the second moment and, by centering, half the variance. There is no constant or linear term in the expansion. No explicit neighborhood radius or remainder constant is claimed.
